Kaitlin Butts Embraces Theater, Humor, and Ambition on New Album 'Hello, Honky Tonk'

Key takeawaysSinger-songwriter Kaitlin Butts is stepping into a new chapter of her career with the release of her latest album, *Hello, Honky Tonk*. Known for her theatrical background and distinct blend of traditional country, Red Dirt, and eclectic pop influences, Butts has spent

Singer-songwriter Kaitlin Butts is stepping into a new chapter of her career with the release of her latest album, Hello, Honky Tonk. Known for her theatrical background and distinct blend of traditional country, Red Dirt, and eclectic pop influences, Butts has spent years building a dedicated following on the road before experiencing a major career breakthrough.

A Creative Leap Grounded in Honky-Tonks and Theater

Drawing inspiration from diverse sources—ranging from the musical Chicago and Disney World’s Country Bear Jamboree to unexpected vocal nods to Nickelback—Butts crafted Hello, Honky Tonk as a character-driven portrait of the patrons who frequent neighborhood bars. The album opens with a spoken-word introduction from Lainey Wilson, welcoming listeners to "Katie B’s Honky Tonk Saloon."

The record features tracks like the debut single "Never Really Mine" and the cheeky "Bacon Naked," written with Natalie Hemby. Butts’ songwriting explicitly leans into humor, vulnerability, and sharp observations about human relationships while remaining fiercely inclusive.

The Viral Turn and Signing With Republic Records

For years, Butts and her band endured the grueling grind of independent touring, playing to small crowds and navigating industry skepticism. That trajectory shifted when her song "You Don’t Have to Die (To Be Dead to Me)" went viral on TikTok, amplified by fellow artists Avery Anna and Ella Langley.

The sudden digital surge caught the attention of major labels, ultimately leading to a recording deal with Republic Records and a series of high-profile opening slots alongside Wilson and Langley. Reflecting on her journey to major festival stages like CMA Fest, Butts remains focused on carving out a wide-reaching career similar to artists who defy strict genre boundaries.

Practical Implications and What Readers Can Verify

  • Release and Label: Hello, Honky Tonk arrives via Republic Records, marking a major milestone for the independent-raised artist.
  • Key Collaborations: The album features contributions and vocal appearances from artists including Lainey Wilson and TJ Osborne of Brothers Osborne.
  • Verification: Readers can review the original feature interview, album details, and further reporting directly through [Rolling Stone](https://www.rollingstone.com/music/music-features/kaitlin-butts-interview-new-album-tik-tok-ella-langley-1235648082/).
